text:
maria: seeing intermittent packet loss between gpu nodes in us-west-2, pods on node-a -> node-b, spikes correlate with tail latency on model-serving pods
aj: which overlay are we using on those clusters? antrea/ovs or calico/encap?
maria: antrea in encap mode, Geneve enabled. MTU is 9000 on nodes but pods show 1500 inside netns
sam: that mismatch screams fragmentation. any logs from NIC/driver? mlx5 on these hosts?
maria: yes mlx5_core, dmesg shows some channel errors around the times of drops. short snippet:
```
[1769123.123456] mlx5_core 0000:83:00.0: FW error detected, resetting
[1769123.124000] mlx5_core 0000:83:00.0: Link flapped
```
kyle: FW resets + Geneve = bad. Geneve adds encapsulation so larger packets might need GSO/GRO cooperation. Try disabling GSO/GRO on the VXLAN/Geneve iface to see if it stops reassembly bugs.
aj: agree. quick test to toggle on one node:
```bash
# on node-a
ip netns exec kube-podns ip link show
ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
```
maria: ran that on a canary node, pod <-> pod p99 latency dropped and few drops for 10m, but not a long term fix
sam: might be firmware bug with offloads + encapsulation. We should capture tcpdump on the host nic and on the veth inside pod to confirm if packets disappear before/after encap.
maria: tcpdump from host shows GENEVE headers then nothing, inside pod we see fragmented TCP segments arriving out-of-order. pasted tcpdump excerpt:
```
12:34:01.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 0, proto UDP) hostA.geneve > hostB.geneve: UDP, length 1600
12:34:01.123457 IP hostA > hostB: Flags [P.], seq 12345:13945, ack 1, win 29200, length 1600
```
kyle: interesting. Also check net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing and net.ipv4.tcp_sack on the hosts. Sometimes PMTU discovery fails with encaps and path MTU ends up wrong.
aj: can also try setting encapsulation MTU in Antrea to account for geneve overhead. BTW how many pods per node? if high density, the CPU for encap/decap might spike -> driver resets.
maria: ~120 pods per gpu node, 2 high-throughput model replicas. CPU on host not saturated but mlx5 offload counters bump.
sam: let's run iperf3 across nodes to characterize UDP vs TCP loss, and a sustained small-packet test to see if it's size-related.
maria: started iperf3:
```
# from node-a to node-b
iperf3 -c node-b -t 300 -P 8
```
results: TCP good at steady throughput but occasional retransmit spikes aligned with the FW error logs
net-bot: detected >5% packet-loss on 10s window between node-a (10.0.12.34) and node-b (10.0.12.67) at 1769123
aj: that aligns. Next steps proposal:
- open support ticket with NIC vendor, include dmesg + tcpdump + timestamped iperf logs
- temporarily set antrea.encapMTU to 1450 and roll on a canary pool
- disable GSO/GRO on one node pair to validate offload interaction
- enable kernel tcp_mtu_probing=1 on affected nodes
- collect perf counters and mlx5 logs for vendor

maria: doing encapMTU change on staging now, will watch for 30 minutes. disabling offloads on node-b too for test
kyle: if vendor patch needed, we may need to fallback to host-routing mode (no encap) for Dedicated clusters to avoid encap path problems. cost of that is more BGP/hostroute churn but acceptable short term.
aj: also consider SR-IOV or DPU-based offload for heavy model-serving nodes to reduce cpu-driven encaps. but long-term architectural change.
maria: update: after encapMTU=1450, p99 latency normalized for 20m, no new dmesg resets yet. leaving it on canary and collecting traces.
sam: great. when you have tcpdump + iperf logs upload to ticket and tag me. I'll draft vendor repro steps.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary change to antrea.encapMTU=1450 applied to pool gpu-canary at 1769123889
aj: nice, keep monitoring. I'll prepare the SR-IOV/DPU TCO calc if vendor says firmware fix will be delayed.
kyle: +1 on that. if we need quick mitigation, schedule a rolling host-routing flip for affected cluster during low traffic window.
maria: noted. I'll post follow-ups in this thread with vendor ticket link and the packet captures.
